title: oscal-validate report
description: The shape of `oscal-validate --format json`. Every report carries `report_schema_version`, which is the version of this document and not the version of the tool. `additionalProperties` is false everywhere on purpose: a consumer that validates against this schema learns about a new key rather than ignoring it.

report_schema_version.description: The version of this schema that the report conforms to. Semantic: the major part changes when a consumer that reads the old shape would break.

version.description: The tool's own version, which moves independently of report_schema_version.

model.description: The OSCAL model at the root of the primary document, e.g. catalog, profile, system-security-plan.

findings.description: Every finding, deduplicated and in the tool's own deterministic order. An empty array is possible in principle and does not occur in practice, because a run always reports the constraints it did not evaluate.

summary.description: How many findings of each severity. Every severity is always present, including the ones that are zero: a consumer must never have to read the absence of a key as a count of none.

baseline.description: Present only when --baseline was given. Absent is not the same as a baseline that acknowledged nothing: a run that was never given one makes no claim either way. `path` is the file as it was named on the command line. `acknowledged` is how many findings in this report an entry matched -- they are still in `findings`, still carry their own severity, and are still counted in `summary`. `stale` is how many BASELINE_STALE findings this report carries, one per entry that matched nothing in this run. Both counts are derived from the findings this report carries, so a report cannot claim an acknowledgement it does not show.

source-line.description: A 1-based line or column in the source file the finding's pointer points into, present on every finding only when --locations was given. Null means this run found no position for that pointer -- a value the walk synthesised, or a document whose source was not indexed. Never 0: there is no line 0 and no column 0, so a consumer never has to read a zero as either a position or an absence. Columns count characters, not UTF-8 bytes. Absent, as opposed to null, means --locations was not given and the run makes no claim either way.

severity.description: ERROR gates the exit code. UNVERIFIABLE never does; it marks what the supplied documents cannot settle, and it is never a pass.

rule.description: The published rule a finding is made under, with the source it was read from and the date it was read. Never a rule written from memory.

url.description: Where the rule was read. A URL for a published rule; for this tool's own stated policy, the document and section that states it.

retrieved.description: The date the source was read, ISO 8601, or "-" where the source travels with the repository and has no retrieval date.

suggestion.description: An identifier that IS declared and is close to one that resolved to nothing. Present only under --suggest, and never a claim about what was meant.

difference.description: What a reader would have to change, in the tool's own vocabulary.

code.description: The stable identifier of what was found.

location.description: An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the primary document, or <path>#<pointer> when the finding is in a document supplied through --resolve.

property.description: The property, constraint target, or datatype the finding is about.

value.description: The value as written, rendered as a string. "(absent)" where the finding is that nothing was written.

suggestions.description: Absent unless --suggest is on and this finding is settled. Absent is not the same as empty: a run without the flag makes no claim either way.

acknowledgement.description: Why a finding was accepted and when, copied from the matching --baseline entry. Absent unless a baseline matched this finding, and its presence is the only thing that distinguishes an ERROR that gates the exit code from one that does not. It changes nothing else: the severity, the message and the counts are untouched.

reason.description: The written reason. A baseline entry without one is refused.

acknowledged_on.description: The date the entry was written, YYYY-MM-DD. Never compared against today: this tool does not read the clock.
